title: A 1939 fair ride flew visitors over a model of America’s 1960 motorways

cover.alt: Faded colour film still: tiny streamlined model cars on a wide, multi-lane model highway that runs along the foot of a rocky cliff.
cover.credit: Jam Handy Organization for General Motors · Public domain

body: At the 1939 New York World’s Fair, General Motors’ **Futurama**, designed by Norman Bel Geddes, imagined America 20 years in the future. Visitors sat in armchairs on a moving conveyor, 552 at a time, and glided along a winding path above a 1-acre animated model of farms, cities and highways. About 10,000 of its 50,000 model cars actually moved, along a 14-lane highway with lanes for different speeds. The exhibit is credited with helping popularise the idea of a national network of interstate highways.

slides.alt: Faded colour film of the Futurama model: small teardrop-shaped cars and trucks move along the parallel lanes of a model motorway beside a cliff, overtaking one another.
slides.caption: From GM’s 1940 film of the exhibit: streamlined model cars and trucks glide along the lanes of a Futurama motorway beneath a cliff.
slides.credit: Jam Handy Organization for General Motors · Public domain · excerpt

slides.heading: What filled the 1-acre model
slides.note: More than 500,000 buildings, each designed individually. Car numbers are approximate.

slides.question: How long did the armchair ride over the model last?
slides.explanation: 18 minutes. The chairs crept along a third of a mile (0.5 km) at about 1.36 mph (2.19 km/h), slow enough to take in the details.

slides.label: visitors a day, the show’s full capacity
slides.text: They inched along in long queues on the sizzling pavement. A survey of 1,000 departing fairgoers scored GM’s show 39.4 points as the most interesting exhibit, against 8.5 for Ford in second place.

slides.prompt: Did the Futurama’s vision of the future come true?
slides.detail: Its highway system is credited with popularising the idea of interstates, and the bills that led to the US Interstate Highway System were reportedly influenced by it.
